entries.name: vphone-cli

capabilities.evidence: The adapter targets Apple Silicon and the host preflight reports architecture.
Boot is available for firmware pairings with recorded compatibility evidence.
Create, boot, stop, pause, resume, clone, and delete are mapped through the typed adapter.
The adapter handles local IPSWs and automatic supported pairings.
CPU, memory, storage, display targeting, audio, and networking are configurable; fidelity remains profile- and guest-dependent.
The lab provides verified export/import snapshots rather than engine-native live snapshots.
VM bundles can be cloned through the adapter.
Display is available, but GPU acceleration and utilization evidence are not available.
Host-backed Virtio input/output is reported; interruptions, accessories, and exact routing fidelity are unavailable.
NAT, bridged, and no-network modes are mapped; proxy and capture require trusted extensions.
Development app deployment is mapped through the guest channel.
Logs, crashes, screenshots, and diagnostics are available; a general guest shell and accessibility tree are not.
Typed workflows, vdlctl, test matrices, and the authenticated queue use the adapter.
iOS 12–15 profiles are research targets without project boot evidence.

notes: This is the only runnable backend in version 0.6.
Availability still depends on host Recovery policy and supported firmware.

entries.name: QEMU research
entries.version: Unpinned — no adapter or redistributed component

capabilities.evidence: QEMU runs on macOS and can use Hypervisor.framework, but no lab adapter has been validated.
iOS work is separate research; this project has no QEMU iOS boot evidence.
Generic QEMU lifecycle exists, but no typed iOS adapter is implemented.
Firmware and boot-chain handling would require a separate reviewed research integration.
QEMU is highly configurable, but iPhone hardware fidelity is unverified.
QEMU supports generic VM state and disk mechanisms; iOS compatibility is unverified.
No lab adapter exists.
iOS graphics/device emulation remains a research problem.
Generic audio backends do not establish iOS audio fidelity.
Generic networking exists, but the proposed iOS profile has not been validated.
No guest deployment channel is integrated.
QEMU research tooling is potentially useful but not connected to the lab.
QEMU is scriptable; the lab has no QEMU adapter.
A research candidate only, with no support claim or automatic fallback.

notes: Shown to guide adapter research, not as an install or launch option.
A pinned component-level license review is required before code or binaries are distributed.
